metadata.description: Curated primary sources for July 2026 time series forecasting: baselines, global/panel forecasting, hierarchical reconciliation, probabilistic evaluation, and TS foundation models. Includes Chronos-2/Chronos-Bolt, Toto 2.0, TimesFM 2.5, TiRex, and fev-bench.
metadata.title: AI Ml Timeseries - Sources

foundations_and_benchmarks.name: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.)
foundations_and_benchmarks.relevance: Canonical reference for forecasting principles, baselines, and evaluation workflows.

foundations_and_benchmarks.name: M5 Forecasting Accuracy Competition
foundations_and_benchmarks.relevance: Benchmark reference for large-scale retail and feature-based forecasting workflows.

forecasting_frameworks.name: statsmodels Documentation
forecasting_frameworks.relevance: Local classical models and decomposition diagnostics.

forecasting_frameworks.name: LightGBM Documentation
forecasting_frameworks.relevance: Official tree-boosting reference used in feature-based forecasting stacks.

forecasting_frameworks.name: MLForecast Documentation
forecasting_frameworks.relevance: Official Nixtla docs for global feature-based forecasting with lags, date features, and static features.

forecasting_frameworks.name: HierarchicalForecast Documentation
forecasting_frameworks.relevance: Official reconciliation docs for coherent hierarchical and grouped forecasts.

forecasting_frameworks.name: skforecast Documentation
forecasting_frameworks.relevance: Official recursive and direct forecasting workflows around tabular regressors. Current version ~0.22.x (April 2026); verify at https://skforecast.org/ before quoting a version number.

forecasting_frameworks.name: AutoGluon Time Series Documentation
forecasting_frameworks.relevance: Official AutoGluon docs for rapid time-series benchmarking, ensembling, and TSFM comparisons.

probabilistic_and_calibration.name: MAPIE Documentation
probabilistic_and_calibration.relevance: Official conformal prediction reference, including current regression and time-series APIs.

foundation_models_and_governance.name: Chronos Forecasting Repository (includes Chronos-2 and Chronos-Bolt)
foundation_models_and_governance.relevance: Official repository for Amazon's Chronos TSFM family. Chronos-2 (released 20 Oct 2025) adds zero-shot multivariate and covariate support and reports a 90.7% fev-bench win rate. Chronos-Bolt (released 26 Nov 2024, not 2025 — verified via the Dec 2024 AWS launch blog) is up to 250x faster and ~20x more memory-efficient than original Chronos. Verify current model card before recommending a specific variant.

foundation_models_and_governance.name: Chronos-2: From Univariate to Universal Forecasting (paper)
foundation_models_and_governance.relevance: Primary source for Chronos-2's reported fev-bench results: 90.7% win rate / 47.3% skill score, ahead of TiRex (80.8% / 42.6%). Cite this paper rather than a secondary blog when quoting the figures.

foundation_models_and_governance.name: TimesFM Repository
foundation_models_and_governance.relevance: Official repository for Google's TimesFM time-series foundation models. TimesFM 2.5 (released Sept 2025) is a 200M-param decoder-only model with a 16,384-step context window and, with the optional quantile head, forecasts up to 1,000 steps — a large jump from TimesFM 2.0's 500M params / 2,048-step context. Chronos-2 and Salesforce Moirai 2.0 have since displaced TimesFM 2.5 at the top of GIFT-Eval; verify the current leaderboard before calling it best-in-class. LoRA fine-tuning via HuggingFace PEFT is documented in timesfm-forecasting/examples/finetuning/.

foundation_models_and_governance.name: Toto — Datadog Time-Series Foundation Model
foundation_models_and_governance.relevance: Toto 2.0 (published to Hugging Face May 2026, not April): multivariate zero-shot TSFM using u-µP scaling. Model family 4M-2.5B params; hyperparameters tuned on the 4M model transfer to the 2.5B checkpoint. Leads BOOM (Datadog's own observability benchmark), GIFT-Eval, and the contamination-resistant TIME benchmark. Verify general-domain fit and current fine-tuning support before using outside observability contexts.

foundation_models_and_governance.name: TiRex / TiRex-2 (NX-AI)
foundation_models_and_governance.relevance: NX-AI's 35M-parameter xLSTM zero-shot forecaster; strong on GIFT-Eval and the second-best fev-bench model behind Chronos-2 (80.8% win rate / 42.6% skill score). TiRex-2 (2026) adds multivariate, covariate-aware, and streaming forecasting in a single checkpoint. Previously unverifiable in this skill's earlier revision — now confirmed via the official repo and model card.

foundation_models_and_governance.name: fev-bench: Realistic Forecasting Benchmark and Leaderboard
foundation_models_and_governance.relevance: 100-task forecasting benchmark (paper: arxiv.org/abs/2509.26468) spanning 7 domains, built from 96 unique datasets; 30 tasks include known dynamic covariates, 24 past dynamic covariates, 19 static covariates. Also ships fev-bench-mini (20 tasks) for cheaper comparisons. Preferred over informal ablations for TSFM comparisons. Python library: fev (github.com/autogluon/fev).

foundation_models_and_governance.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
foundation_models_and_governance.relevance: Governance baseline for high-impact forecasting deployments and operational risk controls.
